text:
owen: Noticing weird behavior in eu-west1: several GPU jobs preempting quickly after start. Nodes show free GPUs but heavy egress. Suspect NIC contention.
sophia: Did we get alerts?
ops-bot: alert 9374: node.egress.pct > 88% on eu-west1 racks 3-5
owen: Example node dump: 
```
$ kubectl top node eu-west1-rack3-node12
CPU% 28  MEM% 40  egress_mbps=710  GPUs=2 free
```
We scheduled a 4-gang job there and it flaked with driver NVLink retries + kubelet eviction of small sidecars.
jules: TL;DR: scheduler only sees GPUs free; it doesn't account for node-level egress. Leads to ghost-free GPUs but unhealthy placement.
sophia: Short term: cordon top noisy nodes and drain non-critical streaming pods to warmpool. I can run: `kubectl cordon <node>` + `kubectl drain --pod-selector='role!=gang'`.
owen: Also consider a transient taint when egress_mbps > 650: `egress-hot=true:NoSchedule`. Ops automation can apply for 2-5m bursts.
jules: Medium term: lightweight scheduler scoring plug-in that penalizes nodes proportional to egress_mbps for pods with annotation `scheduling=egress-aware`. Feature flag canary in eu-west1.
sophia: We should also add rack label `rack.egress=low|med|high` from inventory so scoring can avoid hot racks.
ops-bot: runbook hint: /runbooks/egress-gpu -> cordon noisy nodes; apply egress QoS shaping; consider network isolation.
build-bot: created incident inc-20260306-egress-stranding and checklist entry.
owen: Cost note: observed ~15% more GPU-hours lost to retries during the 4h window. We'll track cost tag in incident.
sophia: I'll own the cordon script + runbook update. Jules, can you draft the plugin KEP?
jules: Yes, will add perf hooks (placement latency, eviction_count, egress_at_place).
owen: OK — immediate action: cordon top3 noisy nodes; then roll a canary scoring tweak. Update thread when cordon done. :thumbsup:
